name: Kimi K2 Instruct
definition: Kimi K2 Instruct is a very-large agentic Mixture-of-Experts model developed by Moonshot AI in the Kimi K2 family. It has 1T parameters with 32B/token active parameters, supports 128K tokens of context, accepts Text / code and produces Text / code. Its primary role is agentic intelligence, coding, tool use and general-purpose assistants.

key_topics: agentic intelligence, coding, tool use and general-purpose assistants

details: 61 layers with one dense layer in the published architecture
384 routed experts, 8 selected per token plus shared expert

training.summary: Moonshot reports 15.5T pretraining tokens for Kimi K2 and emphasizes agentic intelligence, coding and tool use. The Instruct checkpoint is the direct-response post-trained variant rather than a later explicit “thinking” model.

license.name: Modified MIT License
license.classification: Permissive MIT base with additional scale-triggered branding condition
license.special_conditions: If a commercial product/service exceeds either 100M monthly active users or $20M monthly revenue, the published modified license requires prominent “Kimi K2” display in the product/service user interface.
license.legal_note: OpenWeightModels summary for technical comparison; not legal advice.

hardware.summary: The 1T total parameter pool is a major datacenter workload even with 32B active per token. Production serving requires expert/tensor parallelism, fast interconnect and typically reduced precision. FP8 is central to the published checkpoint ecosystem.

limitations: 32B active does not imply a 32B storage footprint.
Autonomous tool use requires sandboxing and permissions.
The Modified MIT license adds a branding condition for very large commercial services.
Long context and agent traces can create high latency/token costs.
